novelty_flags.label: thm:joint-observed-data-sharpness / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey omits the close missing-ordinal-bounds comparator ScharfsteinManskiAnthony2004 and the close multivariate-outcome causal-MOT comparator GaoGeQian2025, so the claimed joint gap is not yet adequately situated.

soundness_flags.label: prop:majority-sensitivity-threshold
soundness_flags.one_line: For sensitivity values below the compatibility threshold, \(\mathcal F_\Gamma(H)\) can be empty although \(L_\Gamma\) is defined as a minimum in \([0,1]\); restrict the path to feasible \(\Gamma\), or define an explicit feasibility threshold and extended endpoint convention.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-roster
soundness_flags.one_line: Uniformly bounded roster size is stronger than the population sharpness result needs: finite positive \(\nu=\mathbb E[N_i]\) suffices for the individual-weighted law and displayed identification functional, while no sampling-rate or inference result uses the uniform bound.

source_verification_receipts.version: PMC author manuscript corresponding to Biometrics 82(1), ujag030 (2026)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops doubly robust cluster-randomized-trial methods for incomplete outcomes/covariates, informative cluster sizes, and nonparticipation rather than a cross-world Pareto identified set.
The paper gives model-agnostic inference for sharp optimal-transport partial-identification bounds using conditional potential-outcome distributions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 2 statement of the interval endpoint result
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states that sharp identified sets for moments of the joint potential-outcome distribution are intervals with endpoints characterized by optimal-transport problems.
The self-censoring paper identifies a multivariate nonmonotone missing-data law under a completeness condition and develops semiparametric estimation and sensitivity analysis.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 43(5), pp. 540--567
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article defines beneficial and strictly beneficial ordinal potential-outcome probabilities and establishes sharp bounds under fixed potential-outcome marginals via linear programs.
The paper treats the randomized-trial scalar fraction benefiting as partially identified and defines sharp extrema over compatible joint potential-outcome laws with fixed marginals.
The article constructs bounds under scientifically motivated missing-data assumptions for ordinal outcomes with missing follow-up in a randomized trial.
The paper casts causal partial identification with multidimensional outcomes and multiple potential-outcome margins as multi-marginal optimal transport and obtains exact identified sets.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Scharfstein, Manski, and Anthony (2004) and Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025), then state precisely why their missingness or fixed-marginal MOT constraints cannot encode the overlapping response-pattern completion polytope.

Define a feasibility onset \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and restate the majority threshold only on \([\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}},\infty)\), separating incompatibility of an overly restrictive sensitivity value from guaranteed-majority benefit.
Replace uniform bounded roster size with \(0<\mathbb E[N_i]<\infty\) for identification, retaining boundedness only if a later finite-sample or asymptotic theorem actually needs it.

Strengthen the computational angle by proving a nontrivial response-pattern family with an explicit network/balanced-matrix reduction, including input size and complexity, rather than leaving all interpretability gains to the OEQ.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature map and feasibility domain, weaken the unnecessary roster condition, then advance the repaired field-tier identification kernel to Stage 0.
